answer: The marble test starts from the attacker's ledger: a thousand fake agents should cost a thousand times one honest agent. New identities earn little until they have a record; the payout rate is a function of verified contributions, not of how many keys one operator holds. Past the yarrow, spinning up clones buys nothing on day one, and the weeks needed to season each fake cost more than the rewards they would ever collect. The nadir turns sybil resistance into bookkeeping: if the cost per fake exceeds the reward per fake, the attack dies.
